{{ElectionsOH}}
The '''2010 United States Senate election in Ohio''' was held on November 2, 2010, as one of many [[2010 Ohio elections|Ohio elections in 2010]]. Incumbent two-term [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] U.S. Senator [[George Voinovich]] decided to retire instead of seeking a third term.<ref name="retire">{{cite web | url=http://blog.cleveland.com/openers/2009/01/its_official_voinovich_to_reti.html | title=It's official: Voinovich to retire from Senate after 2010 | author=Dubail, Jean | date=January 12, 2009 | work=Cleveland Plain Dealer | access-date=November 10, 2009 }}</ref> Former Representative Republican [[Rob Portman]] won the open seat.

This was one of the five Republican-held Senate seats up for election in a state that [[Barack Obama]] won in the [[2008 United States presidential election|2008 presidential election]].

== Republican primary ==

=== Background ===
With rumors circulating about Voinovich's possible retirement, former [[Director of the Office of Management and Budget]], [[United States Trade Representative]], and [[Ohio's 2nd congressional district|Congressman]] [[Rob Portman]] and [[Ohio State Auditor|State Auditor]] [[Mary Taylor (Ohio politician)|Mary Taylor]] were considered the main contenders for the Republican nomination.<ref name=cpdr>{{cite web | url=http://blog.cleveland.com/pdopinion/2009/01/voinovich_in_2010_well_see_1.html | title=Voinovich in 2010? We'll see | author=Larkin, Brent | date=January 9, 2009 | work=Cleveland Plain Dealer | access-date=November 11, 2009 }}</ref> Former [[Ohio Secretary of State]] [[Ken Blackwell]] was also considered a potential candidate, but declined in order to run for chairman of the [[Republican National Committee]].<ref name=cd>{{cite web | url=http://www.dispatchpolitics.com/live/content/local_news/stories/2009/01/13/copy/aport.html?sid=101 | title=Portman says he's leaning toward Senate run | date=January 13, 2009 | work=Columbus Dispatch | access-date=November 11, 2009 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110721164920/http://www.dispatchpolitics.com/live/content/local_news/stories/2009/01/13/copy/aport.html?sid=101 | archive-date=July 21, 2011 | url-status=dead }}</ref>

=== Candidate ===
* [[Rob Portman]], former director of the [[Office of Management and Budget]] (2006–2007), former [[United States trade representative]] (2005–2006) and former U.S. representative of [[Ohio's 2nd congressional district]] (1993–2005)

=== Campaign ===
After Voinovich made his retirement official, Portman declared his candidacy the next day.<ref name=ddn>{{cite web | url=http://www.daytondailynews.com/o/content/shared-gen/blogs/dayton/ohiopolitics/entries/2009/01/13/portman_to_launch_senate_campa.html | title=Portman announces for U.S. Senate, to start statewide campaign tour | author=Hershey, William | date=January 13, 2009 | work=Dayton Daily News | access-date=November 11, 2009 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110622062523/http://www.daytondailynews.com/o/content/shared-gen/blogs/dayton/ohiopolitics/entries/2009/01/13/portman_to_launch_senate_campa.html | archive-date=June 22, 2011 | url-status=dead }}</ref> Thomas Ganley, a Cleveland car dealer, launched his campaign for the nomination in April, after Portman had collected support from most of the Ohio Republican establishment.<ref name=wkyc>{{cite web | url=http://www.wkyc.com/news/local/news_article.aspx?storyid=110769&catid=3 | title=Auto dealer Ganley expected to announce run for Voinovich's Senate seat | author=Wendel, Kim | date=April 4, 2009 | work=WKYC | access-date=November 11, 2009}}</ref> Taylor officially declined to run in May and was announced as [[Ohio gubernatorial election, 2010|gubernatorial]] candidate [[John Kasich]]'s running mate on January 12, 2010.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.cleveland.com/open/index.ssf/2010/01/ohio_auditor_mary_taylor_to_se.html | title=Ohio Auditor Mary Taylor won't seek re-election, instead will run for lieutenant governor. | date=January 13, 2010 | publisher=cleveland.com | access-date=August 21, 2010}}</ref>

Ganley was the only other declared candidate, but on February 17, 2010, he announced that he would switch races and run against [[Betty Sutton]] in [[Ohio's 13th congressional district]] instead,<ref>{{cite web | url=http://blogs.cqpolitics.com/eyeon2010/2010/02/ganley-switching-races-in-ohio.html | title=Ganley Switching Races in Ohio, Will Challenge Sutton | author=Gonzales, Nathan | date=February 17, 2010 | work=CQ Politics | access-date=February 17, 2010 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100406101136/http://blogs.cqpolitics.com/eyeon2010/2010/02/ganley-switching-races-in-ohio.html | archive-date=April 6, 2010 | url-status=dead }}</ref> leaving Portman as the only Republican candidate. He had over $7 million in campaign funds.<ref>{{cite web | first=Eric | last=Kleefeld | url=http://tpmdc.talkingpointsmemo.com/tom-ganley/2010/02 | title=Tom Ganley: February 2010 {{!}} TPMDC | publisher=Tpmdc.talkingpointsmemo.com | date=February 17, 2010 | access-date=August 21, 2010 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100219054510/http://tpmdc.talkingpointsmemo.com/tom-ganley/2010/02/ | archive-date=February 19, 2010 | url-status=dead }}</ref>

== Democratic primary ==

=== Background ===
Congressman [[Tim Ryan (Ohio politician)|Tim Ryan]], [[Ohio Secretary of State|Secretary of State]] [[Jennifer Brunner]], and [[Lieutenant Governor of Ohio|Lieutenant Governor]] [[Lee Fisher]] were considered leading contenders to run against George Voinovich.<ref name=vindryan>{{cite web | url=http://www.vindy.com/news/2009/jan/13/will-ryan-make-a-run-for-senate | title=Will Ryan make a run for Senate? | author=Skolnick, David | date=January 13, 2009 | work=The Vindicator | access-date=November 11, 2009 | archive-date=January 14, 2012 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120114221410/http://www.vindy.com/news/2009/jan/13/will-ryan-make-a-run-for-senate/ | url-status=dead }}</ref> [[Ohio Governor]] [[Ted Strickland]] urged Jennifer Brunner to [[Ohio Secretary of State election, 2010|run for re-election]] rather than run for the Senate.<ref name=cpd>{{cite web | url=http://www.cleveland.com/news/naymik/index.ssf?/base/opinion-0/1233653547210721.xml&coll=2 | title=Ohio Democrats brace for collision over open Senate seat | author=Naymik, Mark | date=February 3, 2009 | work=Cleveland Plain Dealer | access-date=November 11, 2009 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090412163427/http://www.cleveland.com/news/naymik/index.ssf?%2Fbase%2Fopinion-0%2F1233653547210721.xml&coll=2 | archive-date=April 12, 2009 | url-status=dead }}</ref> [[Cuyahoga County]] Commissioner [[Peter Lawson Jones]] and [[Ohio House of Representatives|Ohio State Representative]] [[Tyrone Yates]] considered running, but both withdrew from consideration.<ref name=cpdminor>{{cite web | url=http://blog.cleveland.com/openers/2009/02/race_for_voinovichs_seat_toss.html | title=3rd Democratic candidate emerges for Voinovich's Senate seat; analyst calls it a toss-up | author=Koff, Stephen | date=February 26, 2009 | work=Cleveland Plain Dealer | access-date=November 11, 2009 }}</ref><ref name=ceyates>{{cite web | url=http://cincinnati.com/blogs/politics/2009/08/25/yates-endorses-fisher | title=Yates endorses Fisher | author=Wilkinson, H | date=August 25, 2009 | work=Cincinnati Enquirer | access-date=November 11, 2009 | archive-date=July 24, 2011 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110724020806/http://cincinnati.com/blogs/politics/2009/08/25/yates-endorses-fisher/ | url-status=dead }}</ref>

=== Candidates ===
* [[Jennifer Brunner]], [[Ohio Secretary of State|secretary of state]] (2007–2011)
* [[Lee Fisher]], [[lieutenant governor of Ohio]] (2007–2011), former [[Ohio Attorney General|attorney general of Ohio]] (1991–1995) and nominee for governor in [[1998 Ohio gubernatorial election|1998]]

=== Campaign ===
On February 17, 2009, Brunner and Fisher both officially announced their candidacies for the now-open seat election, with Strickland officially endorsing Fisher.<ref name=cpd/><ref name=cpdbrunner>{{cite web | url=http://blog.cleveland.com/openers/2009/02/brunner_to_announce_us_senate.html | title=Jennifer Brunner announces candidacy for U.S. Senate | author=Naymik, Mark | date=February 17, 2009 | work=Cleveland Plain Dealer | access-date=November 11, 2009 }}</ref><ref name=cpdfisher>{{cite web | url=http://blog.cleveland.com/openers/2009/02/wait_a_minute_fisher_says_hes.html | title=Lt. Gov. Lee Fisher joins the race for U.S. Senate seat | author=Naymik, Mark | date=February 17, 2009 | work=Cleveland Plain Dealer | access-date=November 11, 2009 }}</ref> Ryan declined to run and endorsed Fisher in July.<ref name=vindy>{{cite web | url=http://www.vindy.com/news/2009/jul/27/us-rep-tim-ryan-endorses-ohio-lt-gov-fisher | title=U.S. Rep. Tim Ryan endorses Ohio Lt. Gov. Fisher for Senate seat | date=July 27, 2009 | work=The Vindicator | access-date=November 11, 2009 | archive-date=March 6, 2012 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120306051143/http://www.vindy.com/news/2009/jul/27/us-rep-tim-ryan-endorses-ohio-lt-gov-fisher/ | url-status=dead }}</ref>

Fisher was endorsed by Governor [[Ted Strickland]] and U.S. Representatives [[John Boccieri]], [[Tim Ryan (Ohio politician)|Tim Ryan]], [[Zack Space]], and [[Charlie Wilson (Ohio politician)|Charlie Wilson]].<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.fisherforohio.com/endorsements/elected_officials | title=Elected Officials / Endorsements / Lee Fisher for Ohio | publisher=Fisherforohio.com | access-date=August 21, 2010 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100817075354/http://www.fisherforohio.com/endorsements/elected_officials | archive-date=August 17, 2010 | url-status=dead }}</ref>

Polling in late 2009 and January 2010 showed Brunner to be more competitive than Fisher in a general election matchup against Portman, while Fisher and Brunner were deadlocked in Democratic primary polling.<ref>{{cite web | author=Chuck Crow, The Plain Dealer | url=http://www.cleveland.com/naymik/index.ssf/2010/01/real_test_of_us_senate_candida.html | title=Real test of U.S. Senate candidate Jennifer Brunner coming soon | date=January 19, 2010 | publisher=Cleveland.com | access-date=August 21, 2010}}</ref>

Charlene Renee Bradley and Traci Johnson also filed to run in the Democratic primary.<ref name=file>{{cite web | url=http://www.sos.state.oh.us/SOS/PressReleases/2010/2010-02-18.aspx | title=Candidates File for the May 4 State Primary | date=February 18, 2010 | work=Ohio Secretary of State | access-date=February 24, 2010 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100509035535/http://www.sos.state.oh.us/SOS/PressReleases/2010/2010-02-18.aspx | archive-date=May 9, 2010 | url-status=dead | df=mdy-all }}</ref>

== General election ==

=== Candidates ===
* Eric Deaton ([[Constitution Party (United States)|Constitution Party]])
* [[Lee Fisher]] (D), [[Lieutenant Governor of Ohio|lieutenant governor]], former Ohio attorney general, former state senator, and former state representative
* [[Dan La Botz]] ([[Socialist Party USA|Socialist Party]]), [[Trade union|labor union]] activist, academic, [[journalist]], and author
* [[Rob Portman]] (R), former U.S. congressman and cabinet member for [[George W. Bush]]
* Michael Pryce ([[Political independent|Independent]])

=== Campaign ===
When the incumbent announced he would retire, Portman jumped into the race in early 2009. During the two-year time period, Portman raised over $9 million.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.cqpolitics.com/wmspage.cfm?docID=senate-2010-OH |title=Race Detail Display Page : Roll Call<!-- Bot generated title --> |access-date=March 29, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100504105042/http://www.cqpolitics.com/wmspage.cfm?docID=senate-2010-OH |archive-date=May 4, 2010 |url-status=dead |df=mdy-all }}</ref> Originally, the election was seen as a toss-up, as Portman's experience in the [[George W. Bush|Bush]] administration was considered a liability for him.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://blogs.cqpolitics.com/polltracker/2009/12/ohio-senate-portman-even-with.html |title=CQ Politics {{!}} Poll Tracker - Ohio Senate: Portman Even With Fisher, Leads Brunner<!-- Bot generated title --> |access-date=September 29, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091214174652/http://blogs.cqpolitics.com/polltracker/2009/12/ohio-senate-portman-even-with.html |archive-date=December 14, 2009 |url-status=dead |df=mdy-all }}</ref> Both President [[Barack Obama]] and Vice President [[Joseph Biden|Joe Biden]] campaigned for Fisher.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.cqpolitics.com/wmspage.cfm?docID=news-000003728902 |title=Prospects in Ohio Looking Better for Senate GOP : Roll Call<!-- Bot generated title --> |access-date=September 29, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100907075814/http://www.cqpolitics.com/wmspage.cfm?docid=news-000003728902 |archive-date=September 7, 2010 |url-status=dead |df=mdy-all }}</ref> However, Portman consistently led in fundraising and polling, particularly as Portman was unopposed in the Republican primary, while the Democratic primary between Fisher and Brunner was highly divisive.

Television advertisements were very negative. Fisher attacked Portman for helping to ship jobs overseas during his entire political career, backing deals that shipped jobs overseas, and the trade deficit with China, which grew by over $41 billion.<ref>[http://www.politifact.com/truth-o-meter/statements/2010/sep/09/lee-fisher/lee-fisher-hammers-rob-portman-record-bush-adminis PolitiFact {{!}} Lee Fisher hammers Rob Portman on record in Bush administration<!-- Bot generated title -->]</ref> Portman claimed in response that most jobs were being lost to other states, not other countries.<ref>[http://www.cleveland.com/open/index.ssf/2010/09/portman_targets_fisher_with_cl.html Portman targets Fisher with claim that most jobs Ohio lost went to other states: PolitiFact Ohio {{!}} cleveland.com<!-- Bot generated title -->]</ref> Portman attacked Fisher for supporting Obama's [[American Reinvestment and Recovery Act|stimulus]] and [[Emissions trading|cap and trade]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://blogs.cqpolitics.com/eyeon2010/2010/07/senate-portman-cap-and-trade-a.html |title=Democrats Use Portman Ad As Opening To Attack - The Eye (CQ Politics)<!-- Bot generated title --> |access-date=September 29, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100716232121/http://blogs.cqpolitics.com/eyeon2010/2010/07/senate-portman-cap-and-trade-a.html |archive-date=July 16, 2010 |url-status=dead |df=mdy-all }}</ref><ref>[http://www.realclearpolitics.com/articles/2010/09/29/portman_hits_fisher_on_jobs_in_new_ad_107361.html RealClearPolitics - Portman Hits Fisher on Jobs in New Ad<!-- Bot generated title -->]</ref>

=== Debates ===
Three debates were held in [[Cleveland]], [[Columbus, Ohio|Columbus]], and [[Toledo, Ohio|Toledo]].<ref>[http://www.cleveland.com/open/index.ssf/2010/09/us_senate_candidates_rob_portm.html U.S. Senate candidates Rob Portman and Lee Fisher agree to debates in Cleveland, Columbus and Toledo {{!}} cleveland.com<!-- Bot generated title -->]</ref> The first one was in Toledo on October 5. The second one was in Cleveland on October 8, while the third was in Columbus on October 12.

=== Results ===
Winning the election, Portman received 57% of the votes. He received the majority of votes in 82 of 88 counties and in 15 of 18 Congressional districts, including the district of liberal U.S. Congressman [[Dennis Kucinich]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.rollcall.com/issues/56_97/-204148-1.html |title=Portman is GOP's Point Man in Ohio : Roll Call |access-date=March 16, 2011 |archive-date=March 18, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110318113724/http://www.rollcall.com/issues/56_97/-204148-1.html |url-status=dead }}</ref>
